$doc: Chromium command-line switch sets. Every set is OFF by default. `npm run tune` benchmarks each candidate against baseline and enables a set in config/tuning.json only when it shows a measured improvement on THIS machine and network. Each entry documents what the switch does, why it might help, and its tradeoffs. Never enable a set by hand without benchmark evidence.

baseline.doc: No extra switches. Modern Chromium defaults are already heavily tuned; every candidate below must beat this configuration in A/B benchmarks to be enabled.

no-quic.doc: Disables HTTP/3 (QUIC), forcing TCP + HTTP/2. Hypothesis: on networks that throttle or poorly route UDP, h2 over a warm TCP pool beats QUIC. Target and Walmart sit on Akamai which supports h3, so on healthy networks this should LOSE — the A/B test exists to detect the unhealthy-UDP case. Tradeoff: loses QUIC 0-RTT connection resumption.

gpu-raster.doc: Forces GPU rasterization plus zero-copy texture upload from renderer to GPU memory. Hypothesis: faster paint on image-heavy product grids. Chromium already enables GPU raster on most modern GPUs, so this often measures neutral; on blocklisted or older GPU/driver combos forcing it can regress or glitch. Enable only on measured improvement.

big-cache.doc: Raises the HTTP disk cache to 1 GiB (default is dynamically sized, often 100-300 MB). Hypothesis: the three retailers' image CDNs produce enough cacheable bytes that a larger cache raises the repeat-visit hit rate. Effect only visible on warm/repeat benchmarks over multiple sessions. Tradeoff: disk usage.

no-background-throttle.doc: Prevents Chromium from deprioritizing background renderers, keeping the warm spare renderer and background tabs hot for instant tab switching. Tradeoff: higher CPU and battery usage with many tabs open.
